correctness.rationale: For \(1\le k\le n\), the central hub exists with failure probability at most \(e^{-k/4}\), and a nonneighbor must fall in an endpoint tail. Their count is \(\operatorname{Bin}(n,k/(4n))\); its k-subset union bound is \((e/4)^k\). This yields \(D_n\le Y+1\) without assuming the hub event and tail count independent. The case \(k>n\) is vacuous. Fixed-bin occupancy proves \(\alpha_n\to\infty\), and the uniform geometric tail proves exponential moments and ratio convergence. The verifier exhaustively checked 146598 endpoint pairings by two independent maximum-independent-set algorithms.

value.rationale: Independent kissing number is a natural local intersection-geometry invariant. A uniform exponential additive gap (rather than a ratio-only approximation or a single 2/3 exact-equality event) is a substantive structural comparison between locally visible disjoint packings and the global optimal packing, with all-size constants, model invariance, and justified analytic scaling.
